segments.description: Coaches, please welcome Dr. Mitchell Turner to the Virtual Grants Am Coaches Conference. Dr. Turner is a researcher in the systematic profiling in neurological conditions team at the Edith Cowan University and a sleep consultant at the Mali's Consulting. Mitchell's education background includes exercise and sports science, strength and conditioning and sleep science. Mitchell has recently completed his PhD thesis which aimed to understand the impact sleep-wake behavior and chronotype have on match play and physical performance of tennis players. He is coordinating currently light therapy trials to improve sleep and reduce fatigue for people living with neurological conditions. He has established international collaborations, published numerous peer-reviewed publications and presented at international conferences and invited seminars. Mitchell is passionate about sleep, physical performance and data science. He's a former tennis coach and player but now focuses on improving the performance of others through sleep and chronobiology interventions and education. In today's presentation, Dr. Mitchell talks about the importance of sleep with the tennis performance. Welcome, Dr. Mitchell Turner. Hello, everyone. Thank you for attending my presentation today on the importance of sleep and chronobiology in tennis. First off, I'd like to thank Scott Rawlings and everyone at the Australian Open Coaches Conference
